headline: Stocks claw back losses as yields cool, Jackson Hole looms
body: Equities spent the week fighting elevated Treasury yields and firming oil prices, with the 30-year yield touching its highest level in roughly two decades near 5.3% and crude extending a second straight weekly gain on stalled U.S.-Iran talks. That combination knocked the Dow down more than 700 points Thursday before a Friday rebound pared the damage -- the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each added roughly 0.4% to close the week, and the Dow rallied nearly 1%. Financials led the recovery, and crypto was the standout: bitcoin posted a roughly 22% weekly advance toward the $70,000s on a wave of short-covering, with Robinhood and Coinbase both jumping on the move. The rebound reads more like relief than resolution -- yields eased rather than reversed, and the rate backdrop remains the market's central worry.

Retail chatter leaned toward mega-cap tech and crypto-adjacent names rather than a single populist theme: Nvidia, Amazon and Meta drew heavy mention volume on Reddit's WallStreetBets, while Stocktwits activity clustered around bitcoin, crypto miners and leveraged bitcoin-proxy stocks like MSTR -- consistent with the week's risk-on tone bleeding into speculative corners. Broader positioning gauges point to Greed rather than euphoria, with elevated RSI readings on bitcoin flagged as overbought even as the fundamental catalysts (falling yields, ETF flows) still look constructive. The bigger swing factor sits just ahead: new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote next week, and markets are still calibrating to his communication style after a notably split, hawkish-leaning FOMC.
